references.text: Jabin, the king of Hazor, gathered a coalition against Israel. This verse describes the actual conflict where Madon and Hazor are mentioned together, as summarized in Joshua 12:19.
Joshua captured Hazor and struck down its king with the sword. Hazor was the capital of all these kingdoms, which explains why it is listed among the defeated kings.
Joshua took all the cities of these kings and struck them down with the sword. This includes Madon and Hazor, as mentioned in Joshua 12:19.
Hazor is mentioned again in Judges as a place where the Canaanites had a king who oppressed Israel, showing that the city was rebuilt after Joshua's conquest.
Solomon rebuilt Hazor along with other cities. This demonstrates the continued significance of Hazor in Israel's history following the conquest.
